title: Cap. 7 Rat. 11: equal divine efficacy left to human will is near-Pelagian
pass_a_gloss: Ratio 11. That opinion is to be rejected by us which either is plainly the same as, or at least has a close kinship with, the condemned dogma of the Pelagians: but the opinion of those who state that the death of Christ on the side of the Divine will and intention stands equally toward all as to efficacy, yet on the side of the human will it comes about that in the event it becomes efficacious and fruitful for some, approaches Pelagius as nearly as possible. But the orthodox, awakened by Pelagius to an accurate consideration of this matter, have always taught against him that the fruitful or efficacious application of Christ’s merits depends on the grace of predestination, through which Faith and the good will itself are mercifully conferred on some, which by God’s just judgment is denied to others.
pass_b_english: Ratio 11. We must reject any view that is the same as—or at least close kin to—the condemned Pelagian dogma. Those who hold that on God’s will and intention Christ’s death stands equally efficacious toward all, while on the human will’s side it happens that in the event it becomes fruitful for some, come as near Pelagius as can be. The orthodox, roused by Pelagius to weigh this carefully, have always taught against him that fruitful application of Christ’s merits hangs on the grace of predestination, by which faith and even the good will itself are mercifully given to some and, by God’s just judgment, denied to others.
source_text: Rat. 11. Est ea sententia a nobis rejicienda quae aut plane eadem est, aut saltem arctam habet cognationem cum damnato Pelagianorum dogmate: Illorum autem opinio, qui statuunt mortem Christi ex parte voluntatis & intentionis Divinae aequaliter se habere ad omnes quoad efficaciam, ex parte autem voluntatis humanae evenire, quod in eventu fiat efficax & fructuosa quibusdam, ad Pelagium quam proxime accedit. Orthodoxi autem, ad accuratam hujus rei considerationem a Pelagio expergefacti, & contra semper docuerunt, Fructuosam sive efficacem applicationem meritorum Christi a gratia praedestinationis pendere, per quam quibusdam misericorditer confertur Fides & ipsa bona voluntas, quae aliis justo Dei judicio denegatur.
